findings.claim: The new `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(outputPath), { recursive: true })` sits outside the try/catch used elsewhere in `main`, so any filesystem failure surfaces as a raw unhandled promise rejection instead of the CLI's `Error: <message>` + `process.exit(1)` path.
findings.rationale: The surrounding code deliberately catches errors and prints a friendly message before exiting with code 1. `mkdirSync` can realistically throw: EACCES/EPERM on a read-only or protected parent, ENOTDIR/EEXIST when a regular file already occupies a path segment of the output directory, or ENAMETOOLONG. Because `main` is async and invoked as `void main()`, a throw here becomes an unhandled rejection with a full stack trace rather than the consistent CLI error output (exit code also depends on the Node version's unhandled-rejection policy). Wrapping the mkdir (and ideally the writeFileSync) in the same error handling would keep behavior consistent. Reasonably confident this is a real, if minor, gap; the mkdir itself is otherwise a sensible addition.
